title: R4 with the Kollmorgen TBM2G-11526D at 6:1 (motor study variant tbm_6; study, not adopted)
scope: all configured normal/fault cases for fresh and aged TV banks, four 3-resolution studies, seven paired-heavy uncertainties, support screen at simulated loads

derived.routing_basis: Takeoff tangent at about 37 mm pack radius to guide (~50 mm) plus guide to +Y body exit (~12 mm). Guide contact curvature and exit motion unresolved.

frame_thermal.summary: The motor housing conducts through the stator carrier/pedestal into a 2 mm aluminium base and skin acting as one lumped frame node. The frame loses heat to the room through its exposed outer faces and to the internal forced airflow through its inner faces. The R2 CAD geometry is unchanged; only the interface and the material choice are new.

basis.housing_to_frame_k_w: About 0.05 K/W greased/padded interface over the ~9200 mm² motor face (2000-5000 W/m²K) plus ~0.2 K/W spreading in a 2 mm base, ln(r2/r1)/(2πkt). The RO100 case-to-stator path is unknown and not potted; that is why the upper bound is high.
basis.frame_capacity_j_k: About 0.9 kg of aluminium base and 2 mm skin at 900 J/kg/K.
basis.frame_to_room_w_k: About 0.137 m² of exposed outer area (mounted base face excluded) at ~10 W/m²K natural convection plus black-finish radiation for a 30-40 K rise. Conduction into the board/wall mount is ignored.
basis.frame_to_air_w_k: About 0.15 m² of inner skin at ~10 W/m²K under the conditional 25 CFM internal flow; flow distribution is not demonstrated.

odrive_pro_dc_voltage.note: Extracted table drops empty cells; 15/58 read as min/max. No undervoltage lockout or low-voltage derating is stated.

proposal.basis: The 40 V trip was a reference choice, not a drive limit. 30 V keeps 2x margin above the documented 15 V minimum. Whether the motor can still be controlled at the reached speed is judged by the existing voltage-controllability and modulation screens, which stay unchanged. Usable aged-bank energy from 52 V rises from about 0.5*3.15*(52^2-40^2) = 1.74 kJ to 0.5*3.15*(52^2-30^2) = 2.84 kJ, before ESR losses.
open_items: Supply constant-current limiting means delivered power falls with bus voltage; a constant-power supply mode is not assumed.
Auxiliary/logic rails, sensors and the supervisor must be specified to ride through 30 V.
Low-voltage operation raises bank and wiring currents for the same power; ESR heating is captured, connector/wiring ratings are not.

proposal.basis: In R3 + C1 fast reversal the one-way clamp dumps 317 W of regeneration and the aged bank reaches the 30 V trip. With the bank on the drive bus the fast-motion study dumps 49 W and the aged fast reversal no longer trips. The supply stays one-way and the dump thresholds are unchanged; the overvoltage trip is lowered to 56 V (below).
proposal.trip_basis: Normal operation peaks at the 54.4 V dump level, so 56 V leaves about 1.6 V above normal use and 2 V below the Regen Clamp's 58 V maximum. Chosen instead of replacing the clamp with 80 V-class parts.

reverse_blocking.need: The bus reaches the 54.35-54.5 V dump and up to the 56 V trip, above the 52 V supply setpoint and the EPP-500-54 56 V adjustment maximum. The supply output must not be back-fed.
reverse_blocking.proposal: Ideal-diode (MOSFET OR-ing) controller on the supply output. The model's one-way source assumes it.

precharge.need: The bank is a near short at power-on. The drive must stay disabled until the bank is charged.
precharge.proposal: The bank disconnect closes at power-on and the supply charges the bank through its own constant-current limit (about 24 s to drive enable with a fresh bank). No pre-charge resistor or bypass is used at start-up. The drive is enabled when the bank reaches the enable threshold. The 6.8 ohm pulse resistor remains, as the normally-closed service-discharge path only.
precharge.depends_on: The EPP-500-54 must current-limit continuously into a capacitive load (constant current, not hiccup or shut-down). This is unverified. Normal R4 operation already relies on it, because the heavy and hold cases run the supply at its 9.6 A limit.
precharge.fallback: Resistor pre-charge (sequence B, 120 s fresh) if constant-current mode is not confirmed.

cell_voltage.need: The bank now sees the drive bus maximum. Series cells must stay under rating with imbalance.

dump_monitor.need: With the bank on the bus, a failed dump no longer reaches the overvoltage trip (fresh bank peaks at 55.6 V). Detect it directly.
dump_monitor.proposal: Supervisor compares the shunt-measured dump current with the chopper's gate duty x bus V / R; latches a dump_fault trip.
dump_monitor.duty_source_limit: A gate-driver failure that removes the gate also removes the expected current, so the comparison cannot see it. That failure is left to the 55 V backup threshold and the 56 V trip. The gate signal needs a supervisor input (an isolated or level-shifted tap of the Regen Clamp gate drive); not designed.

ripple_current.need: Bank current now carries drive bus transients. Compared with the cell's 15 K-rise RMS current.
ripple_current.note: Cycle-averaged current only. Drive PWM-frequency ripple is assumed to stay in the drive-bus capacitors; bus wiring inductance is not modelled.

open_items: Verify the EPP-500-54 overload behaviour (constant current vs hiccup) into a capacitive load; it decides the pre-charge circuit.
Select the ideal-diode controller and pre-charge parts; add them to the electrical definition and cost allowances.
Bank wiring inductance, fusing and a bank-disconnect for service are not designed.
Cell balancing (passive or active) is not designed; the worst-cell factor is an assumption.
